# Reference Notes: Corio–Commerce One License and Hosting Agreement

**Parties/Date:** Corio Inc. (Delaware; 700 Bay Road, Suite 210, Redwood City, CA 94063) and Commerce One, Inc. (Delaware; 1600 Rivera Avenue, Walnut Creek, CA 94596). Effective Oct 29, 1999 (signed by Corio's CEO George Kadifa 11/5/99; Commerce One's V.P. Worldwide Sales Mark S. Biestman, date blank). Amendment No. 1 dated March 1, 2001.

**Term (AMENDED):** Original 5-year initial term was changed by Amendment No. 1 to **seven (7) years** from the Effective Date (i.e., to Oct 29, 2006). Then auto-renews for **1-year** periods unless either party gives written notice **at least 30 days** before expiry of the initial term or any renewal. Amendment controls over the original; otherwise unchanged.

**Termination (§11.2):** Material breach uncured **30 days** after written notice; immediate on insolvency or assignment for benefit of creditors. Survival (§11.3): §§4.2, 5.3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14; Corio's customers' existing use rights, and support (if Corio keeps paying annual fees), survive.

**Licenses (§2):** Software = Hosted BuySite v6.0 (object code). Hosting license is fee-bearing, perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except per §14.1), Territory = North America (§1.11); unlimited sublicenses to Customers. Internal-use and demo licenses royalty-free. Distribution/resale right for Commerce One software (§2.4); Commerce One must refer direct Customer inquiries to Corio. Corio Market Segment: customers under **$1,000,000,000** annual revenue (can keep customers that outgrow it). Worldwide expansion: Corio may request; Commerce One not to unreasonably withhold, at no added cost (§2.10). No reverse engineering (§2.7). Commerce One retains ownership (§2.8). End-user terms per Exhibit E.

**Delivery/Acceptance (§3.1):** Test within 30 days of delivery, no later than Dec 1, 1999; Commerce One has 15 days to fix defects; up to three Acceptance Tests; all testing complete by Dec 30, 1999, written notice by Dec 31, 1999. After third failure Corio may repeat the test or terminate with refund.

**Fees (Exhibit B; amounts redacted [*]):** License fee, MarketSite.net access fee, and maintenance fee redacted. Users: unlimited. Revenue sharing: Commerce One pays Corio a redacted % of MarketSite transaction fees; Corio pays Commerce One a redacted % of Application Management Revenue, but none for subscriptions using the initial **3,000** Software User licenses (min. **40** users per Customer); excludes professional services and network fees; accrues at live operations. Implementation: time and materials, capped (redacted). Payment: license and MarketSite access fee due on acceptance (access annually thereafter); maintenance net 30 from acceptance anniversary; revenue share quarterly, net 30 after quarter close; professional services net 30 from milestone invoice. Taxes on Corio except Commerce One income taxes (§4.3).

**Audit (§4.4):** Records kept **3 years**; one audit per calendar year by independent CPA at Commerce One's cost; Corio reimburses if underpayment exceeds **5%**.

**Services:** One full-time operations consultant for 1 week free (§5.1); professional services for first 3 implementations (§5.2); quarterly product meetings (§5.4). Support (Exhibit C): Mon–Fri 7am–7pm PST, 24x7 for Priority 1; contact attempt within 30 minutes of a critical incident; action plan within 2 hours (P1) / 4 hours (P2); up to 5 registered contacts. Updates/Upgrades free of added charge (§3.2).

**Warranties (§7):** Performance/media warranty **60 days** from Effective Date but not past Dec 31, 1999; remedy is repair/replace or termination with refund of prepaid fees. IP non-infringement warranty; Y2K warranty. Implied warranties disclaimed.

**Indemnity (§8):** Commerce One indemnifies Corio and Customers for third-party IP claims; may procure rights, modify, or terminate with pro-rated refund.

**Liability cap (§9):** Except §8, capped at amounts paid by Corio for the relevant transaction in prior **12 months**; no lost profits or consequential damages.

**Escrow (§12):** Agreement within **60 days** of Effective Date; California escrow; Corio pays costs. Release: Commerce One dissolution/ceasing business, or repeated material support breach uncured **60 days**; disputes: 10 business days of negotiation, then arbitration.

**Other:** Developments owned by Corio unless Commerce One supports them (§13.5); mutual patent covenant not to sue (§13.6). Assignment needs consent, except merger/sale of assets, unless the acquirer is a direct competitor (§14.1). Section 365(n) bankruptcy protection (§14.9). Confidentiality via separate NDA. **Governing law:** California; binding AAA arbitration, one arbitrator, San Francisco County; loser pays AAA fees. Notices: personal, fax+courier, overnight (1 day), certified mail (5 days). Initial customers: Corio to seek 2 customers within 60 days (non-binding Exhibit D); marketing fund within 6 months.

# Reference Notes: PcoMed / Integra Supply Agreement (no amendments provided)

**Parties & date:** Integra LifeSciences Corporation (Delaware; 311 Enterprise Drive, Plainsboro, NJ 08536) and PcoMed, LLC (Colorado LLC; 105 S. Sunset St., Longmont, CO 80501). Effective Date May 15, 2013. Signed by PcoMed (Steve Jacobs, CEO) May 15, 2013 and Integra (Brian Larkin, President) May 29, 2013. Affiliates named include SeaSpine and Theken Spine.

**Purpose:** PcoMed applies its surface modification technology (osteoconductive titanium molecular modification of PEEK/PEKK/PAEK) to Integra's implantable spinal interbody/intervertebral devices. Field = spinal interbody/intervertebral surgical methods (fusion, spacer, arthroplasty).

**Exclusivity (§3):** PcoMed grants Integra and Affiliates a sole, exclusive worldwide right to sell/commercialize treated Integra Products in the Field. No right to manufacture with the technology. PcoMed may not sell or license to third parties in the Field. Integra may not apply other coatings (except for identification or sterilization) or impair the technology's integrity (§3.3).
- **Conversion to non-exclusive (§3.2):** If Integra misses Minimum Payments, fails to pay under §2.1-2.3, or otherwise defaults, PcoMed may convert at its sole discretion after written notice and a **45-day cure** period.
- **Territory (§1.27):** Worldwide for 36 months after Notice of Initial Acceptance of First Product Order; thereafter PcoMed may exclude the PRC if Integra has no sales there, on **60 days'** written notice of intent to use a third-party marketer.

**Money:**
- Milestones: first payment on execution; second within 30 days after Notice of Initial Acceptance (amounts redacted). First Product Order due within 60 days of Effective Date. Acceptance notice issued within 10 business days of receiving conforming product.
- Fees: percent of Net Sales of Treated and Partially Treated Products, with a higher or different rate depending on exclusive vs. non-exclusive status at time of sale (all rates redacted). Paid quarterly within **45 days** after quarter end, with a statement. Payments in USD.
- Net Sales deductions: discounts, commissions, returns, taxes/duties, freight/insurance; excludes clinical trial sales.
- Run Fee: flat fee per run (redacted) for max **100** products per run. No Run Fee for regulatory testing quantities (up to a redacted number of units or **four** runs). Due within **30 days** of each run.
- Minimum Payments (Attachment B): seven one-year periods starting at acceptance of First Product Order; amounts redacted. Due annually within **45 days** after period end. Integra uses commercially reasonable efforts; it may satisfy shortfalls by elective cash payment. PcoMed's **sole remedy** for a shortfall is conversion to non-exclusive; Integra has no liability.
- Fee offset: Integra may offset up to a redacted percentage of third-party settlement/license costs caused by PcoMed. Reduced fees still count fully toward Minimums.
- Audit (§6.2): once per calendar year, independent CPA chosen by PcoMed, at PcoMed's cost; results reported within 60 days; underpayments paid within 60 days of agreement or final judgment.
- Taxes (§6.3): PcoMed bears taxes on its receipts; Integra withholds where required.

**Term (§4):** Initial Term runs from Effective Date to the due date of Minimum Payment Period 7 payment. Renewal only by mutual written agreement. Termination for material breach: **60 days'** notice and cure (or an acceptable cure plan). Immediate termination on bankruptcy/insolvency. After early termination (except for Integra breach of §5 or §8), Integra gets an **18-month** sell-off of inventory and committed components. Surviving sections: 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 4.4(c), 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12.

**Confidentiality (§5):** Term plus **20 years**. Agreement terms confidential, with exceptions for legal filings, advisors, and financing/M&A/litigation. Injunctive relief available without bond. Each party submits its own regulatory data to regulators.

**IP (§8):** Each party keeps its own technology. Joint inventions go to PcoMed if primarily relating to PcoMed Technology, and to Integra if primarily relating to Integra Products. PcoMed controls patent filing and prosecution at its expense. Enforcement: PcoMed has first right on matters exclusively about its technology (90 days to respond to Integra's request; Integra may require action if PcoMed fails to act within 90 days or 6 months). Integra has the sole right on other infringement. Declaratory judgment defense: the other party may intervene within 30 days.

**Liability and indemnity:** Mutual exclusion of special, consequential, incidental and indirect damages, except for breaches of §3.1, §5, and §§8.1-8.2. PcoMed indemnifies for infringement from its technology, breach of its reps, and product defects from its technology (Integra's recovery for infringement costs is by fee offset only). Integra indemnifies for infringement from Integra Technology, breach of its reps, and Integra product defects.

**Misc.:** Governing law: **New Jersey**. Disputes: 30-day senior-officer negotiation, then binding arbitration in **Denver, Colorado** (Judicial Arbiter Group, 3-person panel, AAA rules, each side bears own costs). Assignment needs consent, except to an Affiliate or in a merger/sale of substantially all related assets. Force majeure excludes payment obligations. Modifications require a signed, dated writing. Notice to PcoMed's counsel: Alan Keeffe, Sherman & Howard LLC, Steamboat Springs, CO. Integra may state the products were partly manufactured by PcoMed.

# Reference Notes: Purolator / Dynamex Marketing and Transportation Services Agreement

**Agreement:** dated Nov 20, 1995, between Purolator Courier Ltd. and Parcelway Courier Systems Canada Ltd. (subsidiary of Dynamex Inc., "Dynamex"). **Amendment No. 1** dated June 1, 1997 controls over the original where they conflict.

**Term and termination**
- Indefinite term (2.1).
- Without cause (19.1, **as amended**): **12 months** written notice (originally 2 years).
- Change of control of a Party (19.2): the other Party may terminate on written prior notice.
- Default (17.2): 120 days written notice, but immediate on written notice for 17.1(g) (service failures) and (h) (uncured breach).
- Reputation harm (41.1): terminate on notice the other Party deems appropriate.
- Missing Dangerous Goods training certificate (13.2): immediate termination.

**Events of Default (17.1):** bankruptcy petition not dismissed within 60 days; sale of substantially all assets; ceasing business; insolvency or receiver; CCAA proceedings; execution against property; more than 3 Monthly Performance Failures in 12 months (16.1); other breach uncured within 30 days of written notice. Remedies are cumulative (37.1), include recovering monies and repossessing property and Freight, and include set-off (17.4).

**Services and exclusivity**
- Purolator sells sameday service under its own name and tenders all sameday requests to Dynamex.
- Dynamex sells overnight service under its own name and tenders all next-day/multiple-day requests to Purolator.
- Neither may solicit the other's customers (3.5, 3.6), except joint marketing.
- Dynamex may not provide sameday delivery for other next-day/multiple-day carriers (3.9). Exception: Alltours customers, capped at **$5,000/month** revenue, and only if there is no change in control of Alltours.
- Territory: Canada and the US (3.11). Similar agreements with others require prior written consent. Dynamex may contract with others in the US provided it can still serve Purolator.
- DMS and mail room services are carved out (3.10).
- On-time performance of at least **90%**, measured monthly (3.4).

**Payment**
- Currency is Canadian (1.2); business days follow Ontario.
- Invoiced twice monthly (15th and month-end), net **15 days** from invoice date. Invoices must be delivered within 3 days, in duplicate, with supporting documentation (Bills of Lading not required).
- Interest on amounts overdue 30+ days at CIBC (Toronto Main Branch) commercial prime.
- Corrections by debit/credit note, payable net 15 days from receipt and acceptance.
- Services are zero-rated for GST as interlining (Excise Tax Act, Sched. VI, Part VII, s.1).
- Rates are in Schedules D (Purolator pays) and E (Dynamex pays).

**Liability, insurance, indemnity**
- A Party is liable for loss, damage or delay to Freight in its care, custody or control. Not liable if damage is solely from improper packing (6.1).
- Investigation report is due within 30 days (6.2).
- Liability is capped at the Party's liability to its customers: **$4.41/kg or $2.00/lb** unless a higher value is declared (6.3).
- Claims must be paid within **45 days** of documentation, otherwise set-off applies (7.1).
- Mutual indemnity applies even if the indemnifying Party is negligent (8.1). Liability is capped at the insurance coverage in Section 9 (8.2).
- Insurance: cargo liability of at least **$100,000** per occurrence; auto/general/property liability of at least **$2,000,000** per occurrence. Each must name the other as additional insured, with cross-liability and waiver of subrogation. Certificates are due annually, with 30 days' notice of cancellation (9).

**Performance penalty (18.1):** applies after more than 3 failures in 12 months. Penalty = 5 × (90 − actual %) × number of shipments × the other Party's average yield. Example: 5 × (90−85) × 100 × $10 = $250.

**Other terms**
- Non-compete after default termination: **6 months** (42.1). After a change-of-control termination: **12 months** for the Party whose control changed (42.2).
- Dangerous Goods: TDGA compliance required. A Party is liable only if it had actual prior knowledge (13).
- Assignment or subcontracting requires prior written consent (23.1). Strike contingency: subcontract on the same terms (15.1).
- Confidentiality of the entire agreement (34); public announcements must be mutually agreed (38).
- Governing law: **Ontario**; Ontario courts have jurisdiction (36.1).
- Arbitration (39) is a condition precedent to any action. A single arbitrator is appointed within 10 business days, failing which the President of the Arbitrators' Institute of Canada Inc. designates one. Seat is Metropolitan Toronto, costs are shared equally, and the award is final and binding.
- Force majeure (22): written notice required immediately.
- Order of precedence (24.2): Agreement, then Schedules, then operating plan.
- Amendments must be in writing and signed by both Parties (27.1). Time is of the essence (30.1).
- Notice addresses: Purolator, 5995 Avebury Road, Suite 500, Mississauga L5R 3T8; Dynamex, 2630 Skymark Ave., Suite 610, Mississauga L4W 5A4. Mailed notice is deemed received after 5 business days.

**Caveat:** the Amendment is labeled illustrative and not a real filing, but it is treated as controlling here.

# Reference Notes: VIP–BNL Outsourcing Agreement

**Parties:** Virtual Item Processing Systems, Inc. (VIP), 2525 NW Expressway, Ste 105, Oklahoma City, OK 73112 (Oklahoma corp.), provider. Brokers National Life Assurance Company (BNL), 7010 Hwy 71 W, Ste 100, Austin, TX 78735 (Arkansas-domiciled insurer), customer.
**Dated:** Effective May 1, 2006; signed May 17 (VIP, David A. Siekman, President) and May 18, 2006 (BNL, Barry N. Shamas, EVP).
**Amendment No. 1 (Jan 15, 2008)** controls over the original where it conflicts.

**Scope:** EDP services via VIP's proprietary system (new business, policy admin, agency admin, financial admin, claims, vendor provider, transaction tracking, mail tracking). BNL buys its own compatible equipment. Includes one data line and up to 70 devices. VIP may change platform with reasonable written notice and pays BNL's resulting equipment/training costs. VIP owns the system; BNL gets a non-exclusive license during the term.

**Fees:**
- Schedule B: $0.305 per policy per month (all BNL plans). Renewal policies (13+ months from original date) are billed annually/12, paid in advance monthly.
- **Minimum monthly fee: $6,500 from Feb 1, 2008 (Amendment); originally $5,000.**
- Extra line/adapter $200/month; visual station $25; printer under 299 LPM $25; over 299 LPM $150.
- Pass-through costs (forms, phone, postage, COM; travel with prior written approval).
- Invoices due 10 days after postmark; late charge 1.5%/month or the legal maximum, whichever is less.
- New products require a signed addendum.
- Schedule A hourly rates: consultation, development, requirements, analysis $100; senior programmer $100, junior $85; computer time $150; termination services: consultation $100, programming $185, computer time $250; education at VIP $50, on-site $90, phone help $50; bank drafts $0.06 each. After year 1, VIP may raise Schedule A rates on 30 days' notice, capped at 10% per year.

**Term:** Initial term 1 year from May 1, 2006. It then renews year to year unless either party gives 6 months' written notice. If BNL terminates in an Extended Term on under 6 months' notice, it owes a cancellation fee equal to the greatest of: Minimum Fee × remaining months; 6-month average billing × remaining months; or $30,000.

**Termination for cause:** Nonpayment (30-day cure after notice; disputed bills get a meeting first); material breach (30-day cure); insolvency. On termination, data copies cost $100/hr programming and $150/hr processing.

**Service levels:** Available 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Central, Mon–Fri. Downtime over 2 consecutive working days triggers a backup facility at VIP's expense. VIP keeps property/business-interruption insurance and daily off-site backups (BNL pays its pro rata share of storage cost).

**Warranties and liability:**
- VIP warrants: workmanlike services, no infringement, no time-limit programming. All other warranties, including merchantability and fitness, are disclaimed.
- Each party excludes consequential damages. Liability cap for each is fees paid in the prior 12 months for the specific service (in the first year, the minimum fees for 12 months).
- VIP's cap excludes IP infringement indemnity (8(B)) and data confidentiality (6(A)).
- BNL's cap excludes fees owed and VIP proprietary-rights breaches.
- Mutual indemnities (¶8); VIP gives IP indemnity.
- VIP is not liable for the matters in ¶9(G), such as BNL data errors and third-party hardware or software. BNL is solely responsible for security choices.

**Data and confidentiality:** BNL data stays BNL's and is returned on termination. VIP may use it only to render services, and may keep work papers. VIP may use BNL's name in advertising.

**Disputes:**
- **Governing law: Texas (per Amendment; originally Oklahoma).**
- Binding AAA arbitration before 3 arbitrators (one per party, plus a neutral attorney chair); injunctive claims are excepted. The prevailing party recovers attorneys' fees.
- Litigation venue is federal or state court in Austin, TX or Oklahoma City, OK.
- Claims must be brought within 2 years of accrual.

**Other:** No assignment or subcontracting without consent (not unreasonably withheld). Written amendments only. Force majeure for VIP (¶16(J)). Notices by hand, certified mail (deemed given after the stated days, though the text says "three (2)" days, which is ambiguous), or next-day courier. Entire agreement; severability; no third-party beneficiaries; independent contractors. Confidentiality and indemnity survive termination.

# Reference Notes: VerticalNet / Converge Maintenance and Support Agreement

**Parties:** VerticalNet, Inc. (VNI) and VerticalNet Enterprises LLC (VNE, formerly Tradeum, Inc., d/b/a VerticalNet Solutions), together "Vert"; and Converge, Inc. Signed Oct 9, 2001; effective Oct 1, 2001. Tied to the Amended and Restated Subscription License Agreement (SLA). The agreement is automatically terminated if the SLA terminates.

**Amendment No. 1 (Apr 1, 2002)** controls over the original. The only change is that the Initial Term Minimum Fee is reduced from $4,500,000 to **$3,750,000**. Everything else is unchanged. The amendment does not restate the installment schedule, so the $250,000 x 18 figures below are original terms, and the amendment's effect on installments is unspecified. (The amendment says it is illustrative.)

**Term (9.1):** Initial Term runs to March 31, 2003. Renewal only by mutual written agreement, up to three one-year Renewal Terms. Renewal fees are set by agreement (4.2). Work Plans stay in effect until completed.

**Fees (Section 4):**
- Original: 18 monthly installments of $250,000, non-refundable. First is due at signing, then the 1st of each month (Nov 2001 through Mar 2003).
- Other amounts are invoiced monthly in arrears, due 30 days after receipt. Payment is in USD with no setoff. Late charge is the lesser of 1.5% per month or the legal maximum.
- Out-of-scope services are billed at VNE's then-current time charges. Reasonable expenses are reimbursed, but VNE bears travel for Error correction.
- Converge bears Sales Taxes. The withholding gross-up applies if Converge goes foreign.
- Quarterly Allocation (Exh. C): 1,920 estimated hours over 12 weeks, six VNE staff. Problem Reports and Maintenance Updates are provided even above the allocation.

**Support (Section 2, Exhs. A/B):**
- Converge provides Level 1 support; VNE provides Levels 2 and 3. Converge may have at most 7 support personnel without VNE approval.
- Support Hours are 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. ET, Mon–Fri. Phone 1-877-249-1423. Severity 1 and 2 must be reported by phone or in person.
- Severity 1: initial response in 30 minutes (2 hours outside Support Hours), 24x7 efforts, status every 24 hours, final fix in 24 hours.
- Severity 2: response in 2 hours, diagnosis within 1 Support Day, final fix in 72 hours.
- Severity 3: response by end of next Support Day, fix target 5 Support Days.
- Severity 4: diagnosis commencement within 5 Support Days, fix in a future update.
- Converge must install Maintenance Updates, expected within 90 days.
- Delivery is to Massachusetts.
- VNE provides a weekly status log.

**Professional Services (Section 3):**
- Project Managers: Michael Decker (VNE) and Farooq Ahmad (Converge). Relationship Managers: William Swank (VNE) and Francesco DeMarchis (Converge), who must be at director level or higher.
- VNE delivers a Proposed SOW within 45 days of a request.
- The "Environment and Deployment Process" draft is due in 30 days; the final is targeted within 90 days.
- Vert owns Converge-Requested Enhancements, excluding Converge-independent materials, brand features and third-party materials. Converge grants Vert a perpetual license to those excluded materials.

**Warranty/Liability (5–6):**
- Services warranty: industry standards. Breach must be reported within 90 days; remedy is re-performance, within 30 days if feasible.
- All other warranties are disclaimed.
- No consequential damages.
- Cap: for Enhancements, amounts paid for that Enhancement; for Maintenance and Support, amounts paid in the prior 3 months. VNI and VNE share a single collective cap.
- Cap exceptions: bodily injury or property damage from willful misconduct or gross negligence, confidentiality breach, and court-added interest.
- Sole remedy rules split claims between this agreement and the SLA.

**Confidentiality (7):** Standard obligations. The agreement's terms are confidential. SEC filings require redaction and a confidential treatment request (5 Business Days for the other party to identify items).

**Non-solicit (8):** Term plus 1 year. It lapses as to VNE Service Personnel after a Vert Non-Renewal Election.

**Default/Termination (9.2–9.3):**
- Bankruptcy (involuntary proceedings undismissed for 60 days).
- Material breach uncured for 30 days (extendable to 60).
- Converge payment default uncured for 3 Business Days after notice.
- Termination notice must be given within 10 Business Days of the Event of Default.

**General (10):**
- Governing law: US and Pennsylvania; CISG excluded; jury trial waived; 2-year limitation period.
- Assignment to Affiliates is allowed; otherwise consent is required (not unreasonably withheld). A change of Control is not an assignment.
- Force majeure; entire agreement with the SLA; amendments only in a signed writing referencing the agreement.
- Notices: VNI at 507 Prudential Road, Horsham, PA 19044, copy to Michael L. Pillion, Morgan Lewis & Bockius, Philadelphia. Converge at Four Technology Drive, Peabody, MA 01960.
